title: NABH
shortDescription: India's accreditation body for hospitals and healthcare providers — how it differs fundamentally from NABL, and what it actually assesses.
genZNote: Same parent body as NABL. Completely different job.

sections.heading: What Is NABH?
sections.body: NABH — the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers — is India's accreditation body for hospitals and other healthcare organisations. Like NABL, it is a constituent board of the Quality Council of India (QCI) — but it accredits a completely different kind of organisation, against completely different standards.

sections.heading: NABL vs. NABH — Don't Merge These
sections.body: This is the single most important distinction in this entire subject.

rows: Laboratories and lab-adjacent conformity assessment programmes
Assesses against NABH's own hospital/healthcare-specific standards
Focus: patient safety, patient-centred care, and healthcare quality

sections.heading: What NABH Actually Focuses On
bullets: Patient safety — systematically reducing the risk of harm to patients during care.
Patient-centred care — organising care processes around the patient's rights, needs, and experience, not just clinical convenience.
Continuous quality improvement — the same PDCA-style closed loop used across this subject, applied to hospital processes.

Assessment and accreditation of hospitals, as well as certification programmes for other healthcare service types (e.g. smaller facilities, specific departments) — NABH runs more than one programme track depending on the facility's size and type.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: NABH is India's accreditation body for hospitals and healthcare organisations — a constituent board of QCI, focused on patient safety and healthcare quality, entirely distinct from NABL's laboratory-accreditation role.
keyFacts: NABH = National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers.
NABH, like NABL, is a constituent board of QCI.
NABH accredits healthcare ORGANISATIONS (hospitals and related providers); NABL accredits LABORATORIES.
NABH runs more than one programme track for different facility sizes/types, not a single one-size-fits-all standard.
commonConfusion: NABL and NABH share a parent (QCI) and a similar-sounding name, but accredit entirely different kinds of organisations against entirely different standards — they are never the same accreditation.

highYieldFacts: NABH and NABL are both constituent boards of QCI — siblings, not the same organisation.
NABH's core focus areas are patient safety, patient-centred care, and continuous quality improvement.
commonTraps: Using 'NABL' and 'NABH' interchangeably in writing — examiners specifically test this distinction.
mustRemember: NABL → laboratories. NABH → hospitals/healthcare organisations. Same parent (QCI), different domain.

confusedTerms.distinction: NABL accredits laboratories (testing, calibration, medical) against ISO/IEC 17025 or ISO 15189. NABH accredits hospitals and healthcare organisations against its own hospital/healthcare standards. Both are constituent boards of QCI.

possibleQuestions: A hospital wants to improve patient safety, infection control, medication management and patient rights through a healthcare accreditation framework. Which organisation is relevant, and why not NABL?
